example.target: Revisen la pendiente del techo antes de empezar.
example.native: Check the roof pitch before we start.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Foreman to crew: use the ustedes command, revisen.

example.target: ¿Qué material tiene este techo?
example.native: What material does this roof have?

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie. The yo form is irregular: tengo.

example.target: Hoy instalamos tejas asfálticas.
example.native: Today we install asphalt shingles.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. "Vamos a instalar" also means "we are going to install."

example.target: Un obrero mira el techo.
example.native: A worker looks at the roof.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. No "at" word is needed in Spanish: mirar already means "to look at."

example.target: El capataz camina por el techo.
example.native: The foreman walks on the roof.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use "por" for walking across or along a place.

example.target: Instalen el goterón primero.
example.native: Install the drip edge first.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The command for a crew is "instalen".

example.target: Barran la cubierta antes de la sub-capa.
example.native: Sweep the deck before the underlayment.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. The crew command is "barran" (not "barren").

example.target: Luego el capataz ordena: desenrollen la sub-capa.
example.native: Then the foreman orders: unroll the underlayment.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command is "desenrollen".

example.target: Un obrero señala el borde del alero.
example.native: A worker points to the eave edge.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use it when you point to a spot on the roof or the plan.

example.target: El capataz pregunta: ¿Dónde va el goterón?
example.native: The foreman asks: Where does the drip edge go?

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. It is used for asking questions, not for ordering something.

example.target: Nosotros revisamos si hay goteras en la limahoya.
example.native: We check for leaks at the valley.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use revisen (ustedes command) when you speak to the crew.

example.target: La obrera muestra dónde va el tapajuntas.
example.native: The worker shows where the flashing goes.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (muestro). Nosotros keeps the o (mostramos). Muéstrenme is the ustedes command.

example.target: Ellos sellan alrededor de la chimenea.
example.native: They seal around the chimney.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Sellen is the ustedes command.

example.target: Ellos ponen la membrana impermeable por la limahoya.
example.native: They run ice and water shield up the valley.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: pongo. Pongan is the ustedes command.

example.target: El capataz pregunta dónde están las limahoyas.
example.native: The foreman asks where the valleys are.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. It means to ask a question, not to ask for something.

example.target: El ático necesita ventilación.
example.native: The attic needs ventilation.

example.target: La ventilación de caballete va a lo largo de la cumbrera.
example.native: The ridge vent goes along the ridge.

verbs.note: Irregular verb. Use it for where a part goes: «La bajada de agua va aquí.»

example.target: El capataz pregunta: ¿Dónde va la bajada de agua?
example.native: The foreman asks: Where does the downspout go?

example.target: Un obrero la señala en la esquina de la casa.
example.native: A worker points to it at the corner of the house.

example.target: El agua corre lejos de la casa.
example.native: The water runs away from the house.

verbs.note: For water, «correr» means to flow or drain. Regular -er verb.

example.target: Necesito dos cajas de clavos para techo.
example.native: I need two boxes of roofing nails.

example.target: ¿Qué clavos pide el trabajo?
example.native: Which nails does the job require?

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i (pido, pides, pide, piden). Nosotros has no change. Pedir is used for ordering supplies.

example.target: ¿Cuándo los pueden entregar?
example.native: When can you deliver them?

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue (puedo, puedes, puede, pueden). Nosotros has no change. Pueden is the ustedes form, used for a company.

example.target: El proveedor entrega los clavos mañana.
example.native: The supplier delivers the nails tomorrow.

example.target: Por favor, confirmen el pedido.
example.native: Please confirm the order.

verbs.note: The example is a command to ustedes (confirmen). Use it with a supplier's team or a crew.

example.target: Luis dirige la cuadrilla de desmontaje.
example.native: Luis leads the tear-off crew.

verbs.note: Spelling change in yo: g becomes j (dirijo). Other forms keep g.

example.target: ¿Todos entienden el plan?
example.native: Does everyone understand the plan?

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (not in nosotros).

example.target: Cada persona tiene una tarea.
example.native: Each person has an assignment.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: tengo. Stem change e to ie in tú, él, ellos. Not in nosotros.

example.target: Empezamos con el desmontaje a las 7:30.
example.native: We start the tear-off at 7:30.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (not in nosotros). Use empiecen as the command for a crew.

example.target: Avísenme si ven algún peligro.
example.native: Tell me if you see any hazard.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: veo. Other forms are short and regular.

example.target: Quiten todo hasta llegar a la cubierta.
example.native: Tear off everything down to the deck.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Foreman to the crew: use the ustedes command quiten.

example.target: Tiren las tejas al contenedor.
example.native: Throw the shingles into the dumpster.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Ustedes command: tiren.

example.target: Usen la barreta con cuidado.
example.native: Use the pry bar carefully.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Ustedes command: usen.

example.target: ¿Entienden qué hay que quitar?
example.native: Do you understand what must be removed?

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie in every form except nosotros.

example.target: Hoy empieza el desmontaje del techo viejo.
example.native: Today the tear-off of the old roof begins.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie in every form except nosotros.

example.target: La cuadrilla repara la cubierta hoy.
example.native: The crew repairs the deck today.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Command to a crew: reparen.

example.target: El obrero marca el área dañada.
example.native: The worker marks the damaged area.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. In the crew command, c changes to qu: marquen.

example.target: Reemplazamos este triplay hoy.
example.native: We replace this plywood today.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. In the crew command, z changes to c: reemplacen.

example.target: El obrero no cubre el panel blando.
example.native: The worker does not cover the soft panel.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Crew command: No cubran el panel blando.

example.target: El obrero avisa al capataz.
example.native: The worker tells the foreman.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: avisen. Avísenme means 'let me know'.

example.target: Nosotros barremos la cubierta antes de la sub-capa.
example.native: We sweep the deck before the underlayment.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. The ustedes command is barran, which you use with a crew.

example.target: Ellos tiran las tejas al contenedor de escombros.
example.native: They throw the shingles into the debris dumpster.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Tirar also means 'to throw away', which is why it fits the dumpster.

example.target: Un obrero saca todos los clavos viejos.
example.native: One worker pulls out all the old nails.

verbs.note: In the ustedes command, c changes to qu: saquen. The present tense forms are regular.

example.target: Ellos recogen todos los pedazos de teja.
example.native: They pick up all the shingle pieces.

verbs.note: Only the yo form changes: g becomes j (recojo). The ustedes command is recojan.

example.target: Un obrero usa la pala y otro usa la carretilla.
example.native: One worker uses the shovel and another uses the wheelbarrow.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use it for tools: la pala, la escoba, el imán.

example.target: Cubran esta sección antes de irnos.
example.native: Cover this section before we leave.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Crew command: cubran. The past participle is irregular (cubierto), but you don't need it yet.

example.target: Amarren bien la lona con la cuerda.
example.native: Tie the tarp down well with the rope.

verbs.note: Regular verb. Crew command: amarren.

example.target: Detengan el trabajo si cambia el tiempo.
example.native: Stop work if the weather changes.

verbs.note: Irregular: yo detengo. Stem change e to ie (detienes, detiene, detienen). Crew command: detengan.

example.target: Bajamos del techo si cambia el tiempo.
example.native: We come down off the roof if the weather changes.

verbs.note: Regular verb. Crew command: bajen.

example.target: Repetimos el plan para confirmar.
example.native: We repeat the plan to confirm.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (repito, repites, repite, repiten). Nosotros stays regular. Crew command: repitan.

example.target: El capataz mide desde el borde del alero.
example.native: The foreman measures from the edge of the eave.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (mido, mides, mide, miden). Nosotros does not change. Command to a crew: midan.

verbs.native: to run (a line), to mark out

example.target: Los obreros trazan una línea de tiza para la primera hilera.
example.native: The workers run a chalk line for the first course.

verbs.note: Regular in the present tense. Spelling change z to c in the command to a crew: tracen.

example.target: Los obreros empiezan aquí en el alero.
example.native: The workers start here at the eave.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (empiezo, empiezan). Nosotros does not change. Command to a crew: empiecen.

example.target: Ellos ponen la hilera inicial a lo largo del alero.
example.native: They put the starter strip along the eave.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: pongo. Command to a crew: pongan.

example.target: El capataz revisa la medida otra vez.
example.native: The foreman checks the measurement again.

verbs.note: Regular verb. Command to a crew: revisen.

example.target: Escalonen las uniones seis pulgadas, según la guía.
example.native: Stagger the joints six inches, according to the guide.

verbs.note: Regular verb. The crew command is "escalonen". Ask the lead to confirm the real number for the job.

example.target: Revisen las juntas de la siguiente hilera.
example.native: Check the joints on the next course.

verbs.note: Regular verb. Use "revisen" to give the command to the crew.

example.target: Por favor, confirmen la especificación del trabajo.
example.native: Please confirm the job specification.

verbs.note: Regular verb. Add "por favor" when you ask the office to confirm something.

example.target: Las juntas no se alinean en esta hilera.
example.native: The joints do not line up in this course.

verbs.note: Regular verb. In this lesson you often hear it as "no deben quedar alineadas" (must not line up).

example.target: Corten la teja según el patrón del trabajo.
example.native: Cut the shingle according to the job's pattern.

verbs.note: Regular verb. The crew command is "corten".

example.target: Los instaladores instalan el goterón primero.
example.native: The installers install the drip edge first.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. To a crew, the command is instalen. To one person, use usted: instale.

example.target: La cuadrilla empieza el goterón en el alero.
example.native: The crew starts the drip edge at the eave.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie in every form except nosotros. Crew command: empiecen. To one person: empiece.

example.target: El instalador corta el goterón en la esquina.
example.native: The installer cuts the drip edge at the corner.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: corten. To one person: corte.

example.target: El instalador explica la secuencia del goterón.
example.native: The installer explains the drip-edge sequence.

verbs.note: In commands, c changes to qu: expliquen (crew), explique (one person). Use it to ask the installer to walk you through the sequence.

example.target: Los instaladores revisan las instrucciones del fabricante.
example.native: The installers check the manufacturer's instructions.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: revisen. Useful for checking the plan or the label before you answer.

example.target: Desenrollen la sub-capa bien recta.
example.native: Roll out the underlayment nice and straight.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The foreman gives the crew the command with ustedes: desenrollen.

example.target: Sujeten la sub-capa con clavos de tapa plástica.
example.native: Fasten the underlayment with plastic cap nails.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use sujeten when you speak to the whole crew.

example.target: Un obrero mide el traslape otra vez.
example.native: A worker measures the overlap again.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i (mido, mides, mide, miden). Nosotros has no change: medimos.

example.target: El capataz confirma con las instrucciones del fabricante.
example.native: The foreman confirms with the manufacturer's instructions.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use it to check a spec, such as the overlap, against the label or instructions.

example.target: Hoy empiezan con la sub-capa.
example.native: Today they start on the underlayment.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (empiezo, empiezas, empieza, empiezan). Nosotros has no change: empezamos.

example.target: Corten la membrana a la medida.
example.native: Cut the membrane to length.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. To the crew, use the ustedes command: corten.

example.target: Quiten el papel protector del adhesivo.
example.native: Peel the backing paper off the adhesive.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: quiten.

example.target: Por eso la cuadrilla pone protección extra.
example.native: That is why the crew adds extra protection.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: pongo. Crew command: pongan.

example.target: Presiónenla bien contra la cubierta.
example.native: Press it down flat against the deck.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In a command, the pronoun attaches and an accent is added: presiónenla.

example.target: Nosotros mostramos la protección antes de cubrirla.
example.native: We show the valley protection before covering it.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (muestro), except nosotros (mostramos). Crew command: muéstrenme.

example.target: Pedro clava dentro de la franja de clavado.
example.native: Pedro nails inside the nailing strip.

verbs.note: Regular verb. To the crew: «Claven en la franja.» Do not confuse the verb clavo (I nail) with the noun el clavo (the nail).

example.target: El capataz revisa las tejas asfálticas de la hilera nueva.
example.native: The foreman checks the asphalt shingles in the new course.

verbs.note: Regular verb. To the crew: «Revisen cada clavo.»

example.target: Pedro corrige el clavo alto en esta hilera.
example.native: Pedro fixes the high nail in this row.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (corrige). The yo form changes g to j: corrijo. The command for ustedes is corrijan: «Corrijan esta hilera.»

example.target: Los trabajadores mantienen los clavos dentro de la zona de clavado.
example.native: The workers keep the nails inside the nailing zone.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie, and the yo form ends in -go: mantengo. The command for ustedes is mantengan.

example.target: El capataz muestra dónde está la franja.
example.native: The foreman shows where the strip is.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue, except in nosotros (mostramos). The command for ustedes is muestren, and with me it becomes «Muéstrenme dónde está la franja.»

example.target: Revisen las instrucciones del producto antes de definir el patrón de clavado.
example.native: Check the product instructions before setting the nail pattern.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. To the crew, use the command revisen (ustedes).

example.target: Lean la envoltura del paquete.
example.native: Read the wrapper on the package.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. The crew command is lean.

example.target: Necesito el patrón exacto de este producto.
example.native: I need the exact pattern for this product.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use it for questions like ¿Cuántos clavos necesita esta teja?

example.target: Usen el mismo patrón en cada teja.
example.native: Use the same pattern on every shingle.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command is usen.

example.target: Hoy la cuadrilla abre un paquete nuevo de tejas asfálticas.
example.native: Today the crew opens a new package of asphalt shingles.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb. The crew command is abran.

example.target: Ajusten la pistola de clavos.
example.native: Adjust the nail gun.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. A foreman gives this command to the whole crew in the ustedes form.

example.target: Un obrero revisa el compresor y la manguera.
example.native: A worker checks the compressor and the hose.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command uses the ustedes form.

example.target: Bajen la presión de aire.
example.native: Lower the air pressure.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. It also means "to go down" or "to come down," for example off the roof.

example.target: Pongan un clavo nuevo al lado.
example.native: Put a new nail next to it.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (pongo). The crew command uses the ustedes form.

verbs.native: to nail, to drive a nail

example.target: No claven de más.
example.native: Don't over-drive the nails.

verbs.note: The yo form looks like the noun for nail. Context tells you which one is meant.

example.target: Instalen una pieza por cada hilera.
example.native: Install one piece per course.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: instalen (ustedes). To one person: instale (usted).

example.target: Doblen el tapajuntas contra la pared.
example.native: Bend the flashing against the wall.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: doblen.

example.target: El instalador explica la secuencia del tapajuntas.
example.native: The installer explains the flashing sequence.

verbs.note: The c changes to qu in commands: expliquen (ustedes), explique (usted).

example.target: El instalador muestra cómo se traslapa el tapajuntas.
example.native: The installer shows how the flashing overlaps.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (muestro, muestras, muestra, muestran), but not in nosotros (mostramos). Command: muéstrenme.

example.target: El capataz revisa cada pieza antes de colocar la siguiente hilera.
example.native: The foreman checks each piece before placing the next course.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: revisen.

example.target: Corten los caballetes de una teja inicial, si el producto lo permite.
example.native: Cut the ridge caps from a starter shingle, if the product allows it.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The foreman's command to the crew is "corten".

example.target: El capataz revisa también la ventilación de caballete.
example.native: The foreman also checks the ridge vent.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Command to the crew: "revisen".

example.target: Instalen los caballetes a lo largo de la cumbrera.
example.native: Install the ridge caps along the ridge.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Command to the crew: "instalen".

example.target: Sellen el último caballete.
example.native: Seal the last cap.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Command to the crew: "sellen".

example.target: Cuando terminen, limpien el techo.
example.native: When you finish, clean the roof.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Command to the crew: "limpien".

example.target: Nadie sube sin arnés.
example.native: Nobody goes up without a harness.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb. To the crew: «Suban» (go up). «No suban» means don't go up.

example.target: Todos revisan su arnés antes de subir.
example.native: Everyone checks their harness before going up.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command is «revisen».

example.target: Nosotros anclamos el arnés antes de subir al techo.
example.native: We tie off the harness before going up on the roof.

verbs.note: Regular. The reflexive «anclarse» (me anclo, nos anclamos) means to tie yourself off. Crew command: «anclen».

example.target: Cada persona muestra el anclaje aprobado al capataz.
example.native: Each person shows the approved anchor to the foreman.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (muestro), except nosotros (mostramos). Crew command: «muéstrenme» (show me).

example.target: La protección contra caídas solo sirve si cada persona la usa bien.
example.native: Fall protection only works if each person uses it correctly.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: «usen».

example.target: Detengan el trabajo. El anclaje no es seguro.
example.native: Stop work. The anchor is not safe.

verbs.note: Irregular like tener: yo detengo, and e to ie in tú/él/ellos. The crew command is detengan. The reflexive form (detenerse) means to stop oneself: "Se detiene."

example.target: Revisen si la línea de vida tiene daños.
example.native: Check whether the lifeline has any damage.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: revisen.

example.target: La persona competente confirma la distancia de caída del sistema.
example.native: The competent person confirms the fall distance of the system.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: confirmen.

example.target: El obrero se detiene y avisa al capataz.
example.native: The worker stops and tells the foreman.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use it to report a problem: "Avísame si ves daños" (tell me if you see damage).

example.target: Un arnés no sirve si el anclaje o la eslinga fallan.
example.native: A harness is no use if the anchor or the lanyard fails.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. With two subjects (el anclaje o la eslinga), the verb is often plural: fallan.

example.target: Viene una tormenta. Bajen ahora.
example.native: A storm is coming. Come down now.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command is «bajen» (ustedes).

example.target: Detengan el trabajo y bajen si cambia el tiempo.
example.native: Stop work and come down if the weather changes.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie, and «yo» is irregular (detengo). The crew command is «detengan».

example.target: Usen botas con buen agarre.
example.native: Wear boots with good grip.

verbs.note: On the job, «usar» also means to wear gear such as boots or a harness.

example.target: Buscamos un apoyo firme al pisar porque el rocío resbala.
example.native: We look for solid footing because the dew is slick.

verbs.note: Spelling change c to qu in commands: «busquen».

example.target: Bajen si cambia el tiempo.
example.native: Come down if the weather changes.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. «El tiempo» means the weather here.

example.target: Raúl toma agua cada hora.
example.native: Raúl drinks water every hour.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command is tomen (ustedes); to one person, use tome (usted).

example.target: Raúl descansa en la sombra porque se siente mareado.
example.native: Raúl rests in the shade because he feels dizzy.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Commands: descansen (crew), descanse (one person).

example.target: ¿Cómo se siente, Raúl?
example.native: How do you feel, Raúl?

verbs.note: Reflexive, and the stem changes e to ie (siento, sientes, siente, sienten), but not in nosotros. Use se siente with usted.

verbs.native: to let know, to tell, to notify

example.target: Raúl avisa al capataz si se siente mal.
example.native: Raúl tells the foreman if he feels sick.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The command avise (usted) takes an accent when me is added: avíseme.

example.target: Raúl va a la sombra para descansar.
example.native: Raúl goes to the shade to rest.

verbs.note: Very irregular. The usted command is vaya (Vaya a la sombra); for the crew, say vayan. Vamos a seguir means "we are going to follow."

example.target: Ponemos la cinta de precaución alrededor de la zona restringida.
example.native: We put up the warning tape around the exclusion area.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: pongo. The crew command is pongan.

example.target: Todos se alejan de la casa antes del desmontaje.
example.native: Everyone moves away from the house before the tear-off.

verbs.note: Reflexive verb. The crew command is aléjense; for one person, use aléjese.

example.target: Esperamos hasta que el capataz diga que está despejado.
example.native: We wait until the foreman says it's clear.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command is esperen.

example.target: Si usamos el ducto de escombros, avisamos primero.
example.native: If we use the debris chute, we warn people first.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The crew command is avisen.

example.target: ¡Cuidado abajo! ¡Caen escombros!
example.native: Heads up! Debris coming down!

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: caigo. Use caen for plural things, like escombros.

example.target: Los obreros toman una foto antes y después de la reparación.
example.native: The workers take a photo before and after the repair.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. A foreman uses the ustedes command (tomen) with a crew.

example.target: Un obrero muestra el área dañada al capataz.
example.native: A worker shows the damaged area to the foreman.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (muestro), except nosotros (mostramos). Command to a crew: muéstrenme.

example.target: Los obreros reemplazan el triplay dañado.
example.native: The workers replace the damaged plywood.

verbs.note: The z changes to c in the command: reemplacen.

example.target: Un obrero mide la sección y dice la medida.
example.native: A worker measures the section and gives the measurement.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (mido, mides, mide, miden), except nosotros (medimos).

example.target: El capataz revisa la sección reparada antes de cubrirla.
example.native: The foreman checks the repaired section before covering it.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In the passage, "hasta que yo lo revise" uses a special form (revise) after "hasta que".

example.target: Revisen el tapajuntas alrededor de esta ventilación.
example.native: Check the flashing around this vent.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The foreman uses 'revisen' (ustedes command) to give the order to the crew.

example.target: Sellen los clavos expuestos.
example.native: Seal the exposed nails.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use 'sellen' when speaking to the crew.

example.target: Tomen una foto del tapajuntas alrededor de cada penetración.
example.native: Take a photo of the flashing around each penetration.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. 'Tomar una foto' is the usual way to say 'take a photo'.

verbs.native: to walk through / to go over

example.target: Recorremos cada penetración juntos.
example.native: We walk through each penetration together.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. 'Recorramos' (let's walk through) is the nosotros command form, used in the passage.

example.target: El capataz le pregunta al jefe de cuadrilla qué han revisado.
example.native: The foreman asks the crew lead what they have checked.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. It takes 'le' for the person asked: 'le pregunta al jefe'.

example.target: Revisamos las canaletas antes de irnos.
example.native: We check the gutters before leaving.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The foreman's command to the crew is revisen (ustedes).

example.target: Recogemos todos los clavos alrededor de la casa.
example.native: We pick up every nail around the house.

verbs.note: Spelling change in yo: g becomes j (recojo). The command recojan keeps the j.

example.target: Limpiamos el sitio antes de irnos.
example.native: We clean the site before leaving.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Limpiemos means "let's clean."

example.target: Si el contenedor está lleno, aviso al capataz.
example.native: If the dumpster is full, I let the foreman know.

verbs.note: In the command avísenme ("tell me"), the written accent keeps the stress in the right place when me is added.

example.target: Dejamos el patio más limpio que como lo encontramos.
example.native: We leave the yard cleaner than we found it.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Dejar means to leave something behind or in a condition. It does not mean to leave a place; that is irse, as in antes de irnos.

example.target: Mañana terminamos la sección junto a la chimenea.
example.native: Tomorrow we finish the section next to the chimney.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. To the crew, use the command: terminen.

example.target: Agregamos este pendiente a la lista.
example.native: We add this open item to the list.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. The command spelling changes: agreguen (crew), as in agréguenlo.

example.target: Guardamos los materiales restantes en un lugar seguro.
example.native: We store the remaining materials in a safe place.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. To the crew, use the command: guarden.

example.target: Recorremos el techo antes de dar el trabajo por terminado.
example.native: We walk the roof before we call the job complete.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. To the crew, use the command: recorran.

example.target: ¿Qué áreas quedan pendientes para mañana?
example.native: Which areas are still open for tomorrow?

verbs.note: Often used in the third person: queda (one item) and quedan (several items).

example.target: Siempre anclamos el arnés antes de subir al techo.
example.native: We always tie off the harness before going up on the roof.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. As a crew command, use the ustedes form: «Anclen el arnés.»

example.target: El jefe de cuadrilla revisa cada paso de la instalación.
example.native: The crew lead checks each step of the installation.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Crew command: «Revisen el tapajuntas.»

example.target: Detengan el trabajo y bajen si cambia el tiempo.
example.native: Stop work and come down if the weather changes.

verbs.note: Irregular like tener: yo detengo, and e changes to ie in tú, él/ella/usted and ellos/ustedes. Nosotros keeps the regular stem.

example.target: La cuadrilla cubre con una lona la sección sin terminar.
example.native: The crew covers the unfinished section with a tarp.

verbs.note: Regular in the present tense. Crew command: «Cubran la sección con la lona.»

verbs.native: to walk through / to go over (a roof, a site)

example.target: Recorran el techo conmigo antes de dar el trabajo por terminado.
example.native: Walk the roof with me before we call the job complete.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. Use it for a final walk-through before closeout.
